items.title: TUN RuleSet callback Scope ownership
items.defect: releaseRouteSetCallbacks had exactly one caller, Inbound.Close(), and the product close path never calls Inbound.Close(); Scope.Close runs scope.Add entries only. The rule-set kept an observer pointed at a torn-down *Inbound for the lifetime of the process
items.why_it_was_invisible: protocol/tun/callback_lifecycle_test.go called Inbound.Close() directly, which the product never does - a test that verified the wrong object
items.fix: scope.Add(t.releaseRouteSetCallbacksCleanup) at the acquisition, plus closeAutoRedirect so the release precedes the auto-redirect teardown instead of following it

items.title: MASQUE server endpoint teardown ownership
items.defect: ServerEndpoint.Start acquired a device, a TLS config, a listener and an HTTP/3 server; Close released all of them and nothing handed Close to the Scope. A real Box.Close() left the device and the listening socket open
items.found_by: the ownership sweep P0-L01 called for; it returned exactly two hits on the baseline
items.fix: scope.Add(s.Close) at the acquisition in StartStateInitialize, and Close made idempotent with a sync.Once because the Scope and the duplicate-tag loser path in adapter/endpoint/manager.go can both reach it

items.title: constructor-phase system side effects

bridge_index.verdict: already correct and stricter than upstream; the Scope wiring was untested and is now covered by four tests that all fail when the scope.Add inside allocateIndex is removed

auto_redirect.verdict: RegisterAutoRedirectOutputMark is called at the end of NewInbound with no later error edge, and route.NetworkManager is created per-Box in box.go so the claim cannot outlive the Box or collide across Boxes. tun.NewAutoRedirect acquires nothing in the pinned sing-tun fork

items.constructor_scan: 24 candidates, all judged; false positives and reasoning in docs/fork/lifecycle-scope-resource-ledger.md

items.title: Scope.Start x Scope.Close x Scope.Add contract and failure rollback
defects: Add after Close appended to a queue nobody walks again: permanent silent leak
Start returned success for a Scope that closed while the component was starting
a second concurrent Close returned SUCCESS immediately for a teardown that had not finished
items.reachability_proof: box.go:97-100 states Close is exported and an embedder may call it from any goroutine including while Start is still running, which the daemon deliberately allows; and the dynamic sub-scopes in dns/transport/local, service/resolved and the openvpn/openconnect/tailscale resolvers start transports into a scope another goroutine may be replacing
items.fix: open/closing/closed state under the existing mutex plus a closeDone channel; Add on a closing Scope runs the cleanup on the caller's goroutine outside the lock; Start reports the cancellation; Close records the drain result and later callers join it

items.title: close-path error semantics
items.fix: expand each cleanup's result, then filter E.IsClosed/E.IsCanceled per error; real failures still returned; filtered errors reported through the Scope logger so the observation is not lost

items.title: callbacks, watchers, DBus, event observers and background loops
items.done: the Scope-level contract is defined and tested, and the two components in the tree whose Close the Scope could not reach are fixed
items.open: per-component async exit proofs for route/network.go monitors, the systemd-resolved D-Bus transport, protocol/tailscale global hooks, and the openvpn/openconnect read loops

items.title: idle/reuse ownership rather than unconditional Close
items.reason: a real gap, deliberately not attempted: mistaking an active multiplexed stream for idle is worse than the leak, and the work order requires ReferenceManager reuse and idle draining to be left intact
